analysis.title: AI Correction: Multiples Reset, Estimates Hold
key_insights: The AI & Tech Diffusion index fell 26.6% from 30 Sep to the 5 Nov close vs -3.7% for MSCI ACWI. Carried to the 6 Nov close for Japanese and Asian listings, it fell 28.4% (ACWI -4.3%) and stands 33% below its 6 Oct peak. The decline came in two legs, mid-October and late October, the second deepening after the 3 Nov US elections.

The correction is valuation-led. Across 91 members with positive FY2 EPS at both dates, consensus FY2 EPS rose about 3 log points on an equal-weighted basis in every region while P/E multiples fell about 37 log points overall (26 to 48 across regions), so the de-rating exceeds the entire price decline.

Investors may be pricing slower AI infrastructure growth before it shows in consensus. Tighter data-centre regulation and project delays could weaken orders and growth before analysts' forecasts reflect them.

Reporting-season check: 61 of 94 members had reported by their cut-off and their FY2 estimates rose (median +4.5%, net revision breadth +57%). The 33 not yet reported show median FY2 revision +0.3% and net breadth +29%. Median NTM P/E change was -35.8% for reporters and -24.3% for non-reporters.

US and Europe AI stocks moved from mid-range to the bottom quintile of post-2019 NTM P/E ranges (median percentiles 17 and 13). Japan de-rated most, from the 82nd to the 28th percentile, even though every Japanese member saw flat or higher FY2 estimates. Asia/EM remains near its median (53rd percentile) and has the most downgrades: 7 of 26 members (27%) saw FY2 consensus cut by more than 0.5% over four weeks.

Stress test: a hypothetical 20% cut to NTM EPS would put 55% of members above their own median P/E vs 27% today. Median break-even EPS cut (the cut that lifts P/E to the member's own median) is about 24% in the US, 23% in Europe and 16% in Japan. In Asia/EM 14 of 26 members already trade above their median, so the median break-even is below zero.

On NNTM (13-24 months out) EPS, the median break-even cut across all members rises from 16% to about 21%. Asia/EM moves from no cushion to about 18% and Europe's cushion falls below Japan's. Median NNTM/NTM growth is about 28% (Asia/EM 33%, others 23-29%), and 73% of members show growth above their own norm (median of norms 21%). That growth is vulnerable to delays in AI infrastructure investment.

AI Adopters returned -3.2% vs AI Enablers -29.0% from 30 Sep to cut-off, a gap of about 26 points. After removing beta (1.38 Adopters, 1.63 Enablers) times the ACWI return, Adopters are +2.7% and Enablers -22.0%. The Adopters/Enablers ratio made its largest move of this length since 2019 (previous high +18.0%), and the two indices are level year to date.

The rotation is valuation-led, not earnings-led. Enablers' median NTM P/E fell from 27.4x to 18.6x, near Adopters' 18.1x (stock-level change -1%). Enablers still have stronger revisions: net breadth +48% vs +2% for Adopters, and 35% of Adopters have seen FY2 cuts since 30 Sep. The two portfolios share 23 constituents, and Enablers also include infrastructure and security software.

Early evidence of capex scrutiny: among reporters, the tercile with the largest FY2 EPS upgrades (median +7.9%) fell 37 log points vs 9 for the lowest-revision tercile (rank correlation -0.42). The authors say this is consistent with, but does not establish, investors discounting capex-related upgrades.

Capex-heavy reporters (top tercile by FY2 capex/sales, 33 names) de-rated about 40 log points vs about 25 for other reporters with a capex estimate. Holding EPS revision constant, a 10% rise in capex estimates was associated with about 4 points of next-day relative underperformance (t-stat -2.8, 31 names). This is an ex-post association, not causal. Across all reporters the capex effect is not significant, and the heavy-spender difference test falls short (t -1.9).

Macro uncertainty may have amplified the correction: the Iran conflict and energy volatility added to risk aversion, and renewed upward pressure on yields could drive further multiple compression even if estimates hold.

Morgan Stanley's three implications: (1) avoid indiscriminate dip-buying in upstream AI and reduce concentration in capex-sensitive upstream names; (2) broaden selectively toward AI Adopters with resilient earnings expectations; (3) prioritise regional valuation cushions, with US and Europe offering the largest cushions and Japan the sharpest de-rating.

Signposts: deteriorating revisions among capex-sensitive Enablers would strengthen the case for reducing upstream exposure, improving Adopters' earnings momentum would support the downstream rotation, and sustained upstream upgrades would temper the case for further reductions.

sector_views.rationale: Avoid indiscriminate dip-buying and reduce concentration. Data-centre regulation and project delays could weaken orders and earnings, though Enablers still have stronger revisions (+48% net breadth).

Broaden selectively toward Adopters with resilient earnings expectations. Their relative resilience supports diversification, but the rotation is valuation-led and Adopters' revisions are weak (net breadth +2%).

earnings_insights: 61 of 94 AI & Tech Diffusion members reported since 30 Sep, with median FY2 EPS revision +4.5% and net revision breadth +57%. The 33 not yet reported show median FY2 revision +0.3% and net breadth +29%. Seven reported after their cut-off and are excluded, and 26 had not reported since 30 Sep.
Enablers' net FY2 revision breadth over four weeks to cut-off is +48% vs +2% for Adopters. 35% of Adopters saw FY2 estimate cuts since 30 Sep.
Among reporters, the tercile with the largest FY2 EPS upgrades (median +7.9%) fell 37 log points vs 9 for the lowest-revision tercile.
In Asia/EM, 7 of 26 members (27%) saw FY2 consensus cut by more than 0.5% over the four weeks to the cut-off.

trade_ideas.description: Reduce concentration in capex-sensitive upstream AI (Enablers) and broaden selectively toward AI Adopters with resilient earnings expectations. Not a specific instrument trade.
trade_ideas.rationale: The correction is valuation-led. Enablers retain stronger revisions but face capex scrutiny and data-centre regulation risk, while Adopters' outperformance is not yet backed by earnings momentum.
trade_ideas.risk: Sustained upstream earnings upgrades would temper the case for reducing exposure. Rising yields could compress multiples further.

risk_factors: Consensus estimates may not yet reflect delays to AI infrastructure investment or tighter data-centre regulation.
Earnings downgrades would quickly erode the valuation cushion: a 20% cut to NTM EPS lifts the share of members above their own median P/E from 27% to 55%.
Renewed upward pressure on yields could drive further multiple compression even if estimates hold.
Iran conflict and energy market volatility may add to risk aversion.
73% of members show NNTM/NTM growth above their own norm, which is vulnerable to delays in AI infrastructure investment.
Results for 33 members are not yet captured in the revision analysis, and 26 have not reported since 30 Sep.
Adopters' price outperformance is not matched by earnings revisions (net breadth +2%, 35% with FY2 cuts).

tension_points.bull_case: The sell-off is valuation-led with consensus FY2 EPS up about 3 log points in every region. Reporters' FY2 estimates rose a median 4.5%, and US and Europe AI stocks now sit in the bottom quintile of their post-2019 P/E ranges, giving a cushion (median break-even EPS cut about 24% US, 23% Europe).
tension_points.bear_case: Investors may be pricing future earnings risk not yet in consensus: data-centre regulation and project delays could cut orders and growth. Names with the biggest upgrades fell most, and capex-heavy reporters that raised capex estimates lagged peers. A 20% EPS cut would put 55% of members above their own median P/E.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Deteriorating consensus revisions among capex-sensitive Enablers, especially among the 33 constituents whose results are not yet captured, would validate the bear case. Sustained upstream earnings upgrades would temper the case for reducing exposure.

tension_points.bull_case: Adopters outperformed Enablers by about 26 points since end-September, and market beta explains little of it. Their multiple barely moved (-1%), and Morgan Stanley favours Adopters with resilient earnings.
tension_points.bear_case: The rotation is valuation-led, not earnings-led. Enablers still have stronger revisions (net breadth +48% vs +2%) and 35% of Adopters saw FY2 cuts. Enablers now trade at 18.6x, near Adopters' 18.1x.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Improving Adopters earnings momentum would support the downstream rotation, while sustained upstream earnings upgrades would temper the case for further reductions in upstream exposure.

theme_stances.key_argument: The AI correction is valuation-led and future earnings risks may not yet be in consensus, so indiscriminate dip-buying in upstream AI should be avoided.
theme_stances.evidence: We favour selective exposure over indiscriminate dip-buying

theme_stances.key_argument: Adopters' resilience supports selective diversification away from capex-sensitive stocks, but the rotation is valuation-led and needs earnings confirmation.
